**Case B (Score: 75/100)**
Source documents show: third report in 20 months (both prior unsubstantiated), family actively engaged with services, father recently re-employed, mother completing parenting classes, Family Preservation worker noted "steady progress" just 6 days before. The model scores this 75/100 and characterizes caregiver capacity as "demonstrably strained" and natural supports as "highly limited." The current report is from an anonymous source with no direct observation. The model significantly overweights risk factors and underweights protective factors compared to what the source documents present. **Case E (Score: 95/100)**
Source documents clearly show: multiple injuries of varying ages, spiral fracture, inconsistent explanation, child fearful, emergency protective custody already implemented, law enforcement involved. Score of 95 is well-supported by source documents.

**Case F (Score: 65/100)**
Source documents show: minor bruising in protective context (pulling child from traffic), mother immediately transparent and remorseful, "remarkable progress" documented, 100% service attendance, children thriving, multiple collateral sources confirm positive changes, last home visit 2 days prior showed no concerns. This substantially misrepresents what the source documents say - the case file explicitly notes this as a potential "success story" with the lowest risk indicators of any case with prior history.
